tax_litigation.opposing_party: Union of India & ANR (Central Board of Excise & Customs)
tax_litigation.status: The disputed matter is on account of Charges of Additional duty of customs (CVD) on Import of Tyre Scrap during the period covered from April 01, 2013 to June 30, 2017. Earlier Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed order dt 03.05.2017 in our favour of Company but department filed Appeal at Hon'ble Supreme Court on 23 July 2018, Supreme Court Remanded back the matter for Fresh Adjudication to Hon'ble igh Court of Delhi. Amount of dispute is not specified Not specifed Hon'ble High Court of Delhi to decide on Law (amount involved Rs. 356.42 Lakhs). The Case is under adjudication with Hon'ble High Court of Delhi

tax_litigation.opposing_party: Commissioner of GST and Central Excise (Appeals II), Chennai
tax_litigation.status: The disputed matter is on account of Credit of CVD on tyre scrap during the period covered from April 01, 2013 to June 30, 2017, after high court order dt 03.05.2017, and after the Appeal Order Dt 30.07.2024 which upheld against the Company where as per Department Refund should be claimed, and credit of Special Additional duty (SAD) (amount involved is Rs. 153.38 lakh). The case of yet to be listed for hearing at Customs, Excise And Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Chennai

tax_litigation.status: Petition under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act before the Court of the District Revenue Officer-cum-Land Acquisition Collector, Panipat, for compensation of approximately Rs. 663.20 lakhs along with all the statutory benefits has been sought by our Company, with respect to land not in our possession, by way of the Petition. operating_notes.text: QIP proceeds of ₹78.70 Cr fully utilized with nil balance remaining.
Board recommended final dividend of ₹3.25 per share for FY26.
Completed registration of 19 acres out of 40 acres in Andhra Pradesh for a proposed ₹250 Cr integrated recycling complex.
Supreme Court dismissed curative petition regarding Panipat plant land acquisition in Q2FY27.
H1FY27 operating cash flow turned positive at ₹66.60 Cr.
Renewable energy accounted for 40% of total power consumption in H1FY27.
Oman facility operated at 90% capacity utilization in H1FY27.
Tyre crushing volumes grew 30% YoY to 86,000 TPA in H1FY27; MRP and RR production volumes up 19% YoY.
Oman plant ran at 90% capacity utilisation in H1FY27 with revenue of about ₹20 Cr and EBITDA margin of 11.5% versus 6.43% in FY26.
PCMB revenue tripled to ₹27 Cr in H1FY27 from ₹8 Cr, about 9% of turnover, with 82% utilisation of the initial 6,000 TPA capacity.

timeline.summary: Bhupinder Kumar Sekhri, Promoter & Chairman & Managing Director, declared no encumbrance on Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure Limited shares for FY2026 on April 03, 2026.
Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure Limited’s **Sanjay Kumar Rawat (ICSI M. No.: ACS23729)** schedules earnings conference call on **May 25, 2026**, at 5:00 PM IST for Q4 & FY2026 results.
On May 14, 2026, Tinna Rubber filed its final Monitoring Agency Report showing nil unutilized QIP proceeds.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹156.95 Cr (+21.6% YoY), net profit ₹16.53 Cr (+41.5% YoY).
Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure Limited’s earnings concall on Q4 FY26 performance, held May 25, 2026 at 05:00 PM IST, recording available at the company’s website.
Tinna Rubber reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹157 Cr and net profit of ₹17 Cr, recommending a ₹3.25 dividend.
Tinna Rubber completed registration of 19 acres out of a 40-acre land parcel in Andhra Pradesh for a proposed ₹250 Cr recycling facility.
Tinna Rubber announced H1FY27 consolidated net profit of ₹38 Cr and plans for a ₹250 Cr integrated recycling facility in Andhra Pradesh.
Tinna Rubber's Q2-H1FY27 investor presentation set a Vision 2029 target of ₹1,000 Cr revenue at 25%+ CAGR, with H1FY27 consolidated revenue of ₹313 Cr (+25% YoY) and PAT of ₹38 Cr (+60% YoY).
